speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked the Minister for Education whether Temasek Polytechnic and Ngee Ann Polytechnic had carried out any due diligence to check the background and academic qualifications of Mikhy Farrera-Brochez who apparently had the qualifications of APA, APS, MCollT, MS DPSY, DipED and who was later convicted of having forged his educational qualifications, before employing him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This is in line with the practices of the public sector, as well as many private sector companies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: In addition, Mr Brochez demonstrated a good grasp of the subject during his interviews with the polytechnics' management staff, including those with expertise in psychology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These factors led the polytechnics to decide to hire him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: While due diligence may be conducted thoroughly, there is, unfortunately, no system that is able to exhaustively keep out those who are out to lie and cheat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: However, there are practical limits to such checks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Some overseas institutions may not provide their confirmation, citing privacy reasons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We are also mindful of not going to the extremes and risk losing out on valuable talents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Therefore, the role of in-service performance appraisal and regular monitoring is very important in our human resource (HR) practices.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I find it a bit strange that the polytechnics checked the copies with the originals.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, if the original is already falsified, then you are just checking a false document against another false document.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would think that there must be a more robust process in place, where the institution that is keen on hiring should check back with the institution that conferred those certificates in the first place.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On top of that, there could also be a check with character referees that a potential employee would have worked with in the past.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second question is whether Temasek Polytechnic allowed Mr Mikhy Brochez to set up that Child Psychology Clinic where he had access to exceptional children through the clinic because that was what was reported.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Ministry of Education (MOE) verify that?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For the first, she had some queries and suggestions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, that is being done and in progress.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, on the first question, I want to assure Dr Intan Mokhtar that MOE will continue to work closely with our five polytechnics to continue strengthening their recruitment process.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: During that stint in Temasek Polytechnic, he taught four modules for the first-year students, three modules for second- and third-year students, a total of only 85 students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In Ngee Ann Polytechnic, the percentage of the students he taught was about 1.5%.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: His work is concentrated on delivering the modules.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And even for those modules that the students attended, for Temasek Polytechnic, that comprised about 10% of their graduating requirement.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For Ngee Ann Polytechnic, it is even less; it is about 3% of their graduating requirement.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I wanted to ask about the plans that Temasek Polytechnic had for him to set up a Child Psychology Clinic within the polytechnic.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Did he have any part in doing that and did he have any access to young children through that planned clinic?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To the first question posed by Dr Intan Mokhtar, his work was confined to delivering the modules.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But let me check on that and I will come back to the Member.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For the second question, I want to assure Dr Intan Mokhtar and Members that MOE will spare no effort to work closely with our polytechnics, universities and also the Institute of Technical Education to strengthen our pre-employment checks and ensure that the standard of academic rigour is kept by our educators in our institutions.
